name: Min Heap / Max Heap
description: A complete binary tree where each node is smaller (min-heap) or larger (max-heap) than its children. In JavaScript, heaps are typically implemented using arrays. Used for priority queues, top-K problems, and finding K-th largest/smallest elements.

examples.title: Example 1: MinHeap Class Implementation
examples.explanation: Array-based heap: parent at floor((i-1)/2), children at 2i+1 and 2i+2. insert() bubbles up, extractMin() replaces root with last element and sinks down. All operations O(log n).

examples.title: Example 2: Max Heap & Heapify
examples.explanation: MaxHeap is identical to MinHeap but comparisons are reversed. heapify() builds a heap from an unsorted array in O(n) by sinking down all non-leaf nodes. Useful for converting input data without O(n log n) inserts.

name: Top K Patterns (Kth Largest / Smallest)
description: Uses a heap to efficiently track the K largest or smallest elements in a stream or array. For K-th largest, use a min-heap of size K. For K-th smallest, use a max-heap of size K. Reduces O(n log n) sorting to O(n log k).

examples.title: Example 1: Kth Largest Element in Array
examples.explanation: Min-heap of size K always keeps the K largest elements seen so far. When heap exceeds K, remove the minimum. At the end, the heap root is the K-th largest. O(n log k) time, O(k) space.

examples.title: Example 2: Top K Frequent Elements
examples.explanation: Count frequencies first (O(n)). Then maintain a min-heap of size K on frequency. Elements with smallest frequency get evicted. Result contains K most frequent. Time O(n log k), Space O(n) for hash map + O(k) for heap.

name: Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: A tree-like data structure used to store strings where common prefixes share nodes. Each node represents a character, and paths from root to nodes form words. Used for autocomplete, spell check, prefix matching, and word searching.

examples.title: Example 1: TrieNode Class & Basic Operations
examples.explanation: Each character becomes a node. insert() creates new nodes as needed. search() checks if word exists and is marked as end. startsWith() checks prefix existence without requiring end-of-word. All operations O(L) where L = word length.

examples.title: Example 2: Word Search II (Trie + DFS Backtracking)
examples.explanation: Build trie from word list. DFS from each board cell, following trie paths. Mark visited with '#'. Store word at terminal node to avoid repeated traversal. Time O(m * n * 4 * 3^(L-1)), Space O(N * L) for trie.

name: Merge K Sorted Lists (Heap Pattern)
description: Merges K sorted linked lists (or arrays) by always extracting the smallest/largest element from a heap containing the front of each list. Demonstrates the classic heap use case for conquer/merge problems.

examples.title: Example 1: Merge K Sorted Linked Lists
examples.explanation: Push first node of each list into min-heap. Repeatedly extract minimum, advance that list's pointer, and push the next node. Always processes the smallest available element. Time O(N log k) where N = total nodes, k = lists. Space O(k) for heap.

examples.title: Example 2: Task Scheduler (Greedy + Heap)
examples.explanation: Max-heap processes most frequent tasks first. After executing a task, it goes into a cooldown queue for n time units. When cooldown expires, push back into heap. Time O(m log m) where m = unique tasks. Space O(m).
